reviews.title: Glitches Cost Us Hundreds
reviews.text:
OurPact’s basic screen‑time management works fine, but the app has some serious reliability issues. Several of my child’s app settings repeatedly revert to “Always Allow,” and the “Disable In‑App Purchases” feature randomly turns itself off. After 10 months of using this app, these glitches have cost our family nearly $500 in in‑app purchases I believed were blocked.

I reached out to the developer multiple times, but instead of troubleshooting, they insisted my child “must” have my password or access to my devices and was overriding the settings. That simply isn’t the case, and it was frustrating to have the blame shifted back onto us rather than the app’s functionality being addressed.

At this point, I can’t recommend OurPact. Don’t waste your time or money. We’re switching to Bark, hoping for a more reliable and accountable solution.

reviews.title: A necessity
reviews.text: We’ve been using our pact since 2021 when our oldest got a phone, and now use it for all three of our kids phones. I won’t tell someone how to parent, but will definitely recommend not allowing your child under 16 to have access to the internet. It’s an endless supply of information that can be traumatizing to a child. Social media is the worst thing for a kid. This app allows you to block all of that. Personally don’t like the premium +, as we tried it for two months. We put in specific words that were supposed to be flagged, but never were. The screen shots are useless as you child has to open the app when requested. So don’t bother with the extra subscription. You can utilize the $6.99 by blocking apps, setting schedules and check locations(if you don’t share location with your kids). We love the schedule feature, it’s beneficial for discipline and responsibility. I recommend this app highly and think everyone that has a kid with a phone should use this. We dropped one star because of the premium + subscription, wish it worked as described.

reviews.title: Unworkably bad
reviews.text: I rue the day that I first heard about this app.  My son and I had grown tired of Apple's atrocious Screen Time feature and were both looking forward to something that would allow us a more refined measure of control and OurPact seemed to fit the bill nicely.  Unfortunately, this software is broken and unreliable in ways that are difficult to count.  Even installing the Device Management stub on the client phone took weeks due to a series of issues that renders it unable to be installed from a Mac of even moderately recent vintage.  Once past that, there are so many issues with buggy, broken, nonsensical or flat out poorly implemented features that after hours of struggling with getting things set up properly, my son had a device that had been both reset and crippled and there was nothing that could be done via the parental control app that could address any of these issues.  On the positive side, I found their support department to be helpful, professional and easy to work with.  Unfortunately, there was little they could do in the face of software that was so poorly implemented.  My son and I are now back to Screen Time and just gritting our teeth.

reviews.title: Feels Like a Scam — Hijacked My Kids’ iPads
reviews.text:
I spent half a day trying to install OurPact Premium on my kids’ iPads — struggling through endless compatibility issues with iTunes, PC setup, and their OurPact Connect tool, just to enable “supervision” mode.

Then everything went sideways:
	•	It changed the wallpaper on both devices without any consent or warning.
	•	It removed nearly all apps from the home screen — even the ones that were supposed to be available during scheduled time. I had already created a proper schedule, yet any app not marked “Always Allowed” just disappeared.
	•	I had no idea what was going on — it looked like the devices had been wiped or hacked.
	•	Even worse, it reinstalled random old apps that I had deleted years ago from my account — suddenly showing up on my kids’ devices, unrequested and unwanted.
	•	The device behavior was so extreme and unexplained that I seriously thought this app was a scam or malware.
	•	The forced wallpaper still hasn’t reverted, even after uninstalling everything.
	•	I then had to spend another full hour cleaning up the mess: removing supervision via PC, restoring app visibility, deleting the extra apps it added, and sitting down with my child to explain what just happened.

All I wanted was a simple, responsible way to manage screen time. Instead, OurPact acted like it hijacked our iPads, giving me no control and no clear way out until I manually reversed every step.

This app should come with a big warning label. On iOS, it’s invasive, glitchy, and completely unfit for real-world family use.

I truly thought I was being scammed — and I still don’t understand why any of this is considered normal functionality. Avoid at all costs.

reviews.title: I’ve used it for Years
reviews.text:
Anyone with a child who has their own cell phone needs this app. It works exceptionally well on iPhone. Occasionally there are bugs with screen mirroring but other than that it’s quick and responsive to changes. From your phone to theirs you can make adjustments which show up on their phones within 10 seconds. 

This app and others like it are so important in these times we are in. Don’t want them on socials? Block it. Don’t want them on their phone all night long? Set schedules for bedtimes, homework, and remove time as punishment. It’s all that easy and you don’t have to fight them for the phone just turn it off.
